subject: civil
audience: FE Civil candidates and civil engineering students
title: The Truss Diagonal That Carried More Than the Support Reaction
featured_title: THE TRUSS DIAGONAL THAT CARRIED MORE THAN THE SUPPORT REACTION

presentation.challenge: Each support reaction was only 6 kN, yet each inclined top member carried about 8.49 kN.

practice.primary_question: Why can an inclined truss member force exceed the vertical support reaction it helps carry?
practice.typical_exam_trap: Equating an inclined member's axial force directly to its vertical component.

case_dna.target_misconception: If each support reaction is 6 kN, each inclined truss member at the loaded joint must also carry 6 kN.
case_dna.why_plausible: The 6 kN reaction is the required vertical force contribution on each side in a symmetric truss.
case_dna.contradicting_evidence: For 45° inclined members at the apex, 2F sin45°=12 kN, giving F=8.49 kN in compression.
case_dna.corrected_model: A truss member carries axial force along its own axis. Resolve that force into components at the joint before comparing it with external forces.

problem_statement: A symmetric triangular truss spans 6 m and has an apex 3 m above the supports, so each inclined top member is at 45°. A 12 kN downward load acts at the apex. By symmetry the support reactions are 6 kN each. A review then labels each diagonal member as 6 kN. Determine the actual axial force in each inclined member and identify whether it is in tension or compression.

gates.label: Incident
gates.heading: The support reaction was 6 kN. The diagonal force was not.
facts: Two identical 45° inclined members meet at apex
gates.prompt: What vertical component must each inclined member provide at the apex joint?

options.label: Resolve each axial member force: 2F sin45°=12 kN
options.reason: The vertical components of the two member forces balance the applied load.

options.label: Set each member force equal to 6 kN
options.reason: Six kilonewtons is the vertical component required from each side, not the total force along a 45° member.

options.label: The members must be in tension because they support a downward load
options.reason: At the apex, the required member forces push upward on the joint, indicating compression in the top members.

gates.label: Predict
gates.heading: Predict the inclined member force
gates.prompt: What is the magnitude of each 45° member force in kN?

gates.label: Experiment
gates.heading: Solve the apex joint
gates.result: Each inclined top member carries about 8.49 kN in compression.

gates.label: Gap
gates.heading: Prove the member force
gates.success: F=12/[2sin45°]≈8.49 kN. Its vertical component is 6 kN.

gates.label: Evidence
gates.heading: Joint equilibrium separates axial force from vertical support

cards.text: Symmetry requires each side to contribute 6 kN vertically at the apex.
A 45° member with axial force F contributes F sin45° vertically.
F=6/sin45°≈8.49 kN; the force direction at the apex indicates compression.

gates.label: Redline
gates.heading: Correct the truss-member note
report: C1. The apex load is 12 kN.
C2. Each support reaction is 6 kN.
C3. Therefore each inclined member force is 6 kN.

claims.label: C3
claims.reason: The axial member force must be larger than its 6 kN vertical component at 45°.

evidence_choices.label: 2F sin45°=12 gives F≈8.49 kN
evidence_choices.reason: This is equilibrium of the apex joint.

correction.template: Each inclined top member carries about {force} kN in compression.

gates.label: Design Fix
gates.heading: Reduce the axial force in the inclined members
gates.constraint: Keep the 12 kN apex load and symmetric two-member support at the apex.

options.label: Increase each member angle to 60° above horizontal
Reduce each member angle to 30° above horizontal
Keep 45° and relabel the member force as 6 kN
options.reason: The force components must still satisfy joint equilibrium.

gates.label: Transfer
gates.heading: Apply method of joints
gates.prompt: Two identical 60° members support a 10 kN downward load at a symmetric joint. What is the force magnitude in each member?

options.label: 5.00 kN
options.reason: That is only the vertical component required from each side.

options.label: 10.00 kN
options.reason: This ignores the geometry of two members.

gates.explanation: At a symmetric joint, the two vertical member-force components balance the applied load.

gates.label: Sign Off
gates.heading: Sign off the truss joint
gates.confirmation: I confirm that truss-member axial forces must be resolved into components at each joint.

items.label: What failed
items.value: The member axial force was set equal to its vertical contribution.

items.label: What was assumed
items.value: Support reaction magnitude and diagonal member-force magnitude were treated as identical.

items.label: Corrected model
items.value: Use method of joints and resolve axial member forces along the member directions.

seo.seo_title: Truss Member Force: Why a 6 kN Component Needs 8.49 kN | FE E-043
seo.meta_description: Solve FE Civil Case E-043: a symmetric 45° truss carrying 12 kN develops 8.49 kN compression in each inclined member.
seo.excerpt: An inclined truss member can carry more axial force than the vertical reaction component it provides.
seo.direct_answer: At the symmetric apex joint, the two 45° member forces must satisfy 2F sin45°=12 kN. Therefore F≈8.49 kN in each inclined member. Each contributes 6 kN vertically, while the full axial force is larger.

faqs.q: Why is the truss member force greater than 6 kN?
faqs.a: Because 6 kN is only the vertical component of the inclined axial force.

faqs.q: Are the inclined top members in tension or compression in this case?
faqs.a: Compression; their forces must push upward on the loaded apex joint.
